title: collectReward is a publicly-mempool MEV bait: searchers can sandwich a yield-accumulator deposit to capture rewards intended for long-term stakers
rootCause: When the yield-accumulator (the documented expected funder per the natspec) calls `collectReward(amount)`, two things happen visibly in the mempool: (1) the funding transaction is in flight, (2) immediately after it lands, `rewardBalance` jumps and `rewardPerSecond` is re-anchored upward. Because (a) `stake` is permissionless / capital-only (no whitelist), (b) `withdraw` is also instant with no exit fee, and (c) `accStablePerShare` is updated against the current `totalStaked` at the moment `_updatePool` runs, an MEV bot can: stake immediately before the `collectReward` lands (or in the same bundle, right before), then withdraw + claim immediately after, capturing a disproportionate slice of the just-deposited rewards.
economicImpact: Long-term honest stakers receive less of every `collectReward` deposit than they would under a fee or commit period. Effective APY for buy-and-hold stakers is depressed by the MEV bot's share. The yield-accumulator's deposits leak value to MEV searchers rather than the staking pool the protocol intends to incentivise.
affectedParties: Long-term stakers (lose share of each reward injection); the protocol's stated APY (overstates effective yield); MEV bots gain.
attackScenario: Yield-accumulator (or any funder) signals or schedules a `collectReward(X)` call (e.g., a weekly drip).
MEV bot sees the pending `collectReward` in the mempool. It stakes a large amount in the same block, slot ordered just before `collectReward` lands.
`collectReward` runs: (a) `_updatePool` accrues nothing new (just-staked), (b) `rewardBalance += X`, (c) `rewardPerSecond` recomputed.

On the very next block, the bot calls `withdraw(all)` -- `_updatePool` accrues `rewardPerSecond * 1 block / PRECISION` (which after the V1 re-anchor is non-trivial because rewardBalance is now large), the bot's pro-rata share of that accrual flows to it.
Over many such cycles, the bot extracts a fraction of every `collectReward` injection roughly equal to its capital share of totalStaked at that block.
Sophisticated variant: bot uses a flash loan of phUSD if the staking asset is liquid enough on AMMs, capturing rewards with zero capital lockup.
profitability: Profit per `collectReward(X)` cycle ~= `X * (bot_stake / (bot_stake + honest_stake)) * (Δt/depletionDuration)` over the holding window minus gas. Because the V1 re-anchor concentrates payouts in early blocks after a `collectReward` (the rate is highest right after a deposit and asymptotically decays), the bot's optimal hold is short -- making this a clean sandwich.
preconditions: Reward funder broadcasts `collectReward` to the public mempool (true in default RPC paths).
`stake`/`withdraw` are open and have no holding-period requirement.
Bot has phUSD or can borrow it cheaply.

intentMismatchEvidence.documentation: Natspec on `collectReward` says 'Anyone with approved tokens can contribute rewards' and 'rewards from yield-accumulator contract'. The implied beneficiary is the stable pool of long-term stakers, not arbitrage capital.
intentMismatchEvidence.implementation: No holding period, no withdrawal fee, no anti-MEV mechanism (commit/reveal, private mempool, EIP-712-signed funder). Profile §8.10 already notes this as standard MasterChef behavior.
intentMismatchEvidence.discrepancy: While 'standard MasterChef behaviour' is usually noted as acceptable, the V1 rate-re-anchor bug (CODE-001) materially worsens this: rewards are concentrated right after each `collectReward` (the rate is highest there and decays), so the MEV reward per dollar of capital is larger here than in vanilla MasterChef.

mitigations: Gate `collectReward` to a trusted funder address (the yield-accumulator) via a whitelist, eliminating the public-mempool signalling.
Use a private/MEV-protected RPC for the yield-accumulator's funding transactions.
Add a withdrawal lock or fee on stakes younger than some threshold, with proceeds flowing back to long-term stakers.
Use a 'staking score' (time-weighted) to compute reward shares so freshly-staked capital does not capture freshly-deposited rewards in the same block.
crossReferences: CODE-008 (collectReward(1) griefing) - distinct economic angle: CODE-008 is the funder-side griefing (depress yields), ECON-003 is the staker-side MEV theft (redirect yield). Both share permissionless `collectReward` as root.
